title: De-duplication preserves clause value
statement: Let $t$ be a term over the variables $x_0,\dots,x_{n-1}$, that is, a list of literals, and let $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ be an assignment. Suppose $t$ contains no two literals on the same variable with opposite polarities. Let $t'$ be the term obtained from $t$ by scanning it and keeping a literal only when no earlier-kept literal uses the same variable, so that each variable of $t$ occurs at most once in $t'$. Then $t'$ and $t$ have the same value as a clause under $x$: some literal of $t'$ is satisfied by $x$ if and only if some literal of $t$ is.
hypotheses_covered: term t (list of literals over n variables)
t has no contradiction: no two literals share a variable with opposite polarity
replaced:
For a non-contradictory clause $t$, de-duplication preserves the disjunctive (clause)
value: $\mathrm{CNF.evalClause}\,(\mathrm{dedupTermVar}\,t)\,x = \mathrm{CNF.evalClause}\,t\,x$.
